passageLocation.openingWords: My world had for some years been in Lowood

text: My world had for some years been in Lowood: my experience had been of its rules and systems; now I remembered that the real world was wide, and that a varied field of hopes and fears, of sensations and excitements, awaited those who had courage to go forth into its expanse, to seek real knowledge of life amidst its perils.

curation.context: In Chapter X of Brontë’s 1847 novel, Jane considers leaving Lowood and entering a wider, unknown world.
curation.rationale: The passage opens a field between rules and experience, hope and fear, courage and peril. Its language of width, movement and knowledge supports poems of departure and self-discovery.
